title: REITs
objectives: Answer out loud: Why not use P/E for a REIT?
Answer out loud: What's a cap rate?

steps.body: Real Estate Investment Trusts must distribute at least 90% of taxable income as dividends, avoiding corporate tax.
GAAP depreciation on real estate understates performance, because properties often hold or gain value.
Key metrics: FFO, AFFO, NAV, cap rate.

blocks.template: REITs must distribute at least {{1}} of taxable income
FFO = net income + real estate D&A − {{1}}

blocks.title: What's FFO and why use it?
blocks.teaser: Funds from operations adds back real estate depreciation (which doesn't reflect real value loss for buildings) and removes one-time gains from proper…
blocks.body: Funds from operations adds back real estate depreciation (which doesn't reflect real value loss for buildings) and removes one-time gains from property sales. It's a better measure of recurring cash earnings. P/FFO replaces P/E.

blocks.title: AFFO vs. FFO?
blocks.teaser: AFFO (adjusted FFO) also subtracts recurring maintenance CapEx and adjusts for straight-line rent.
blocks.body: AFFO (adjusted FFO) also subtracts recurring maintenance CapEx and adjusts for straight-line rent. It's closer to the cash actually available for dividends.

blocks.title: What's NAV?
blocks.teaser: Net asset value: estimate the market value of each property (NOI ÷ cap rate), sum them, and subtract debt.
blocks.body: Net asset value: estimate the market value of each property (NOI ÷ cap rate), sum them, and subtract debt. REITs often trade at a premium or discount to NAV.

blocks.title: What's a cap rate?
blocks.teaser: Net operating income ÷ property value — the unlevered yield on a property.
blocks.body:
Net operating income ÷ property value — the unlevered yield on a property. Lower cap rate = higher value (similar to an earnings yield). Cap rates rise when interest rates rise.

**Interview answer:** "NOI divided by property value — the property's yield. A lower cap rate means a higher valuation."

blocks.prompt: A property has NOI of $5M and is valued at $100M. What's the cap rate, and what happens to value if cap rates rise?
blocks.explanation: $5M ÷ $100M = 5%. A higher cap rate means a lower value for the same NOI (like a higher earnings yield).
